delights: It told me when it failed instead of hiding it: slot 3 shipped with "Tried 5 recipe(s) for this slot, none fit within tolerance — closest was \"Chilli ginger lamb chops\" (landed 839 kcal vs a 722 target)." I trust a planner that admits a miss.

Keto and my five walls were both genuinely respected: the day landed 2589 kcal against a 2608 target with carbs at 30g (5% of kcal), and not one of the 14 ingredients across all 5 slots names egg, dairy, gluten, peanut or soy.

The alternates were real, labelled with an honest match %, and one was a dish I would actually cook: "Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts" at matchPct 99 — 797 kcal, 40g protein, and the slot warning cleared when I took it.

defects.what: I asked for a SINGLE day and the first meal of it cannot be eaten for two to three days — it is a cured dish, not a breakfast.
defects.snippet: Sledz w Oleju (Polish Herrings): "Soak herring in cold water for at least 1 hour." ... "Refrigerate for 2 to 3 days before eating."

defects.what: Both of my snack slots are the exact same dish, and before I swapped, meals 2 and 3 were also the same dish — so my day was 3 distinct recipes across 5 slots.
defects.snippet: snack#0 "Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate" — Beef jerky 30g | Pork rinds 15g / snack#1 "Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate" — Beef jerky 30g | Pork rinds 15g

defects.what: 35 grams of vegetables in an entire 2589 kcal day, with essentially zero fibre. I train 150 minutes nine times a week on keto — no greens means cramps and no potassium or magnesium.
defects.snippet: Onion 8g | Garlic 3g | Ginger 13g | Lemon Juice 7g | Parsley 4g (the complete plant total for the day)

defects.what: Every food record carries empty allergen data, so my coeliac and soy walls rest entirely on whether a banned word appears in the food's NAME. "Beef jerky" (eaten twice a day here) and "Chicken Stock" are the two most common hidden soy-sauce and wheat vectors in a supermarket, and neither carries a gluten-free or soy-free flag.

My profile contradicts itself and nothing flagged it: my goal weight is 0.1 kg ABOVE my current weight (maintain), yet it has a 1.5 lb-per-week loss rate applied. You cannot cut 1.5 lb/wk toward a goal above your start weight, and 2608 kcal is several hundred under what 22.5 hours of weekly cardio costs me.
The swap endpoint rejected the recipeId it had just handed me, with an error describing a problem I did not cause.
defects.snippet: HTTP 400 {"error":"a slot needs at least one ingredient"}

defects.what: $43.49 for one day of food — about $1,300 a month for one person — driven by two lamb-chop servings and a $6.75 snack that is 45g of dried meat.
defects.snippet: "name":"Chilli ginger lamb chops","costPerServing":12.83 / "Jerky & Pork Rinds Snack Plate","costPerServing":6.75

defects.what: The plan arrived with no shopping list attached, so I could not see what to buy without generating one separately.

followUp.action: Asked for alternates on the third meal — the duplicate lamb chops that also carried the tolerance warning — and swapped in the one I liked
followUp.howItWent: Alternates were genuinely good — three options, all clean of my five walls, each with an honest match % and its own warning where it did not fit, and I took "Chicken with saffron, raisins & pine nuts" at 99%. The apply call first threw a 400 saying "a slot needs at least one ingredient" when I sent the recipeId it gave me; resending the full alternate object worked, the warning cleared, and a fresh read of the plan confirmed the swap held at 2589 kcal for the day.

verdict: Nothing on this plan can make me ill and the keto maths is genuinely accurate, but as a day of eating it is barely food — a breakfast I cannot touch for three days, the same jerky plate twice, 35 grams of vegetables, and $43 spent to get there.
